sentences.text: 1. The petitioner seeks quashing of case FIR No. 66/2017 of Police Station Mayur Vihar Phase-1 for offence under Section 498A/406/34 IPC on the ground that the complainant de facto (respondent no. 2) has compromised the dispute with the petitioner.
2. Learned APP assisted by IO/ASI Ved Prakash accepts notice and strongly objects to this petition.
3. Respondent no.2 identified by IO also accepts notice.
4. Keeping in mind the nature of disputes I spoke with the respondent no.2 in Hindi.
The respondent no.2 submits that when she came to know that petitioner was already married to someone else, she along with her child left the matrimonial home.
Respondent no.2 submits that she does not wish to live with the petitioner.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 30/03/2026 at 22:45:59 5.

Further, it is quite unpleasant to note that the mediator who recorded the mediation settlement dated 28.05.2024 in the Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Court, Delhi, did not notice that neither the stridhan of respondent no.2 has been returned nor any lump sum settlement amount covering her alimony has been paid.
Moreover, the mediator did not even care to examine any maintenance provision for child of the parties and simply left it to the respondent no.2 to institute maintenance proceedings.

sentences.text: At this stage, at request of learned counsel for petitioner, matter is adjourned because petitioner wants to pay a reasonable amount to respondent no.2 towards her alimony, stridhan as well as maintenance of the child.
7. As requested, relist on 19.05.2026 in Advance List.
8. It is made clear that there is no stay on proceedings of the trial court.
GIRISH KATHPALIA, J MARCH 30, 2026/ry
